prompt:
Produce exactly one concise caption: one sentence of 10–25 words that states only visually verifiable facts. Include 2–6 discrete facts drawn from the following fixed order; omit any item that is not clearly visible.

Order of facts (use this sequence if present):
1) Legible text or logos: if any prominent text/logo is readable, transcribe the exact characters in double quotes and give its location (e.g., Sign reads "London 2012" above banner). If illegible, omit text.
2) Counts and object types: use numerals (e.g., 2 people, 1 bicycle) and canonical object names (sign, person, child, adult, bicycle, bench, table, ball, net, goal, badge, lanyard, brochure, chair, car, storefront).
3) Color/material/texture for those objects (attach modifiers to the object, not as separate facts).
4) Pose/action/orientation (use dynamic verbs and indicate midair/grounded and left/right/toward/away when visible).
5) Simple spatial relation(s) using foreground / midground / background and left / right.
6) Lighting / viewpoint / occlusion cues (e.g., bright sunlight casting long shadows; elevated vantage).

Fact-count rules: transcribed text/logo = 1 fact; each "numeral + object type" = 1 fact; color/material modifiers do not count separately if attached to an object; pose/action = 1 fact; spatial relation = 1 fact; lighting/viewpoint = 1 fact. Total facts must be between 2 and 6.

Additional rules:
- Use numerals for counts and normalized directions (left/right/foreground/midground/background).
- Permit role or scene labels (e.g., goalkeeper, vendor) only when visually supported; immediately follow the role with the visible evidence that justifies it in parentheses (e.g., goalkeeper (gloves, full-size net behind)).
- Mention small, scene-defining objects (ball, net, badge, knife, brochures) when they are clearly visible and relate them to people or furniture.
- Do not infer emotions, intentions, or nonvisual attributes; do not use metaphors, marketing language, or hedging (no "appears to be", "seems", "maybe").
- Keep wording compact; avoid filler conjunctions and long subordinate clauses. Use commas or semicolons to separate facts; do not produce lists, tags, JSON, multiple sentences, or multiple candidates.

Micro-examples:
Good: "Sign reads "Outdoor World" above entrance; 2 adults walk toward entrance; timber façade; overcast sky."
Bad: "A happy farmer enjoys a sunny day in the countryside."
Good (role justified): "Goalkeeper (gloves, full-size net behind); 1 player in red jersey diving midair to the right toward ball; grass field."
Bad (role unjustified): "Vendor handing out brochures" — unless brochures and a table with staff badge are visible.

Produce a single, one-sentence caption that obeys all rules above.
